source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide whether tiny moving beings in pond water or soil suspension are microorganisms when they cannot be seen with the unaided eye.
node_labels: Living systems: organisms, health and ecosystems

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: This nonliving soil grain is a microorganism because it is visible only under the microscope.

mx.teacher_note: Microorganisms occur only in water, not in moist soil.

mx.teacher_note: These stationary microscopic living beings are not microorganisms.

intelligence.enrichment: Microorganisms are very small living beings that cannot be seen with the naked or unaided eye. Pond water, stagnant water, and soil suspension can contain tiny organisms that become observable with a microscope or foldscope. Sampling pond water or soil suspension and using magnification -> tiny organisms become visible -> they can be identified as microorganisms. The learner correctly applies this rule: Microorganisms are very small living beings that cannot be seen with the naked or unaided eye. Pond water, stagnant water, and soil suspension can contain tiny organisms that become observable with a microscope or foldscope. If water or soil only looks like dirt to my eye, any moving specks under a microscope are not living organisms.
